items.title: Lorraine Feather interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 22, 2023
items.q: And I might sing in unison with Charlie Bisharat, the violinist

ctx.x: There was an interesting moment in your tune, “I Love You Guys” where I think it was just the first two lines that you sang. The piano was playing the melody with you and I wondered, I don’t know if it was planned or was it spontaneous but it was a nice effect and you don’t usually hear it because singers don’t usually want that. Do you recall that? © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

Yes. I had forgotten, but you’re right. It is a nice effect that we use sometimes. And I might sing in unison with Charlie Bisharat, the violinist, or with the pianist, in that case it was Shelly. He — I know that at the beginning of that tune he wanted it to be about journeymen musicians who are doing all these gigs and a lot of them were horrible. And he wanted to sound like he was kind of in a lounge overplaying. But we had a lot of fun. I really like it. Oh and then there’s a line in “I Love You Guys”, “I…

That’s an interesting thing to think about inside. Have you ever listened — had your music playing with a small group of people and you’re there and some of these lyric things you do come up. Do you watch these people to see if they’re sort of chuckling at the parts that you hope they chuckle to?
